## Critique
- claim-1: The formulas and specialization data are correctly grounded. The excerpt itself states the two sets but does not independently establish their generating property; that dependency must remain attributed to the accepted generation result.
- claim-2: Supported by accepted task 132 for this specific finite case: the degreewise free ranks sum to \(6\), and all torsion factors vanish. No all-parameter conclusion follows.
- claim-3: Correct. Here \(q=i+p=4\), \(r=j+c=7\), \(n=11\), and \(a=b=2\). Both interval enumerations contain exactly the six displayed partitions. Each generating family induces a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\to\mathbb Z^6\), hence an isomorphism. Moreover, every generating set of \(J_{2,5}\) must map onto \(\mathbb Z^6\) and therefore contain at least six elements. Thus both six-element families are minimum-cardinality and irredundant. The stated strategy reaches the requested target relative to the accepted inputs.

## Required revisions
- Explicitly attribute generation to the accepted generation theorem rather than to the bounded excerpt alone.
- Add the arbitrary-generating-set lower bound above if “minimal” is intended to mean minimum cardinality.

The requested \(i=j=p=2,\ c=5\) minimality corollary is established relative to the accepted project results.
